General, is it true that the HVO's artillery or these particular weapons were deployed in support of Tuta's men in the operation on Rastani?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the artillery, the anti-aircraft gun, 14.5 millimetres, well, that's not the artillery in the classical sense of the word. It's a machine-gun of slightly greater calibre than the 7.9, which is the classical one that infantrymen carry with them. And I have no reason to doubt the report of Mr. Mico Lasic because it's a comprehensive report. It says what the targets are and so on and so forth in very precise terms. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, the next -- or skipping down a bullet point, there's a reference to the PAM 14.5 at the graveyard firing position at Orlac. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, going back to the one -- going back to the one we were just at that -- under number 1 there's a couple different bullet points, and if you look at the fourth bullet point under paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: "The PAM 14.5 at the graveyard firing position at Orlac is a new south-east Herzegovina operative zone weapon that arrived from the HV, Croatian Army, through pilot Bato Sunjic, who is one of Orlovac Company." General, were you aware that the HV Croatian Army was supplying weapons to the South-east Herzegovina operative zone that it was using in its military operations during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This wasn't sent by the Croatian Army. It came from the Croatian Army, and obviously the pilot Sunjic brought it. What was done, that is correct, Mr. Stringer, that people tried to come by weapons in all manner of ways. So if you say that this is -- that somebody in the Croatian Army ordered that weapons be given, that certainly was not true. But that Sunjic happened to bring in an anti-aircraft gun, 14.5 millimetres, that is obviously correct. And it was used at targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that's it. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you don't know how he got this from the Croatian Army?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then skipping down another three bullet points, this is the third bullet, the top of page 2, there's a reference to the 20/1 Oerlikon Pact, and it said that this one fired on facilities in the north camp. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It acted at the military position Kop. And then north camp, it is a 20-millimetre gun with one barrel. You have one barrels, two barrels, four barrels. This one obviously has one barrel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And it says, going on, that this weapon was received by the operative zone from the Croatian Army through Mr. Ivica Mandic, commander of the Pula military post who provided a PAT crew commanded by Mr. Revic, all of this agreed with Mr. Mijo Jelic and Mr. Cule. So again, General, would it be correct to say that you don't know actually how they obtained this weapon, but it appears the weapon was obtained in some way from the Croatian Army?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not obtained from the Croatian Army. When you Croatian Army, obtained from the Croatian Army, then that means that somebody issued an order to that effect, that weapons belonging to the Croatian Army, et cetera, et cetera. That's what it means. Now, whether this was a private contact that led to this or not, I don't know. But this is how both the BH Army and the HVO procured weapons in all possible ways. I assume that's clear to you by now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, before my learned friend poses his next question, may I just remind the Registrar that my learned friend asked for five minutes to address Your Honours before we end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. So maybe we should stop him now, because I see that it's already 20 to 2.00. We can continue on Monday, Mr. Stringer. We'll have plenty of time for that. So I will hand the floor now to the person who wished to intervene. I believe it was Ms. Nozica. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you very much. May we move into private session for the request I have to make?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar.

utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So now that we're back in open session, I would like to mention that we will resume on Monday at 2.15 p.m., and I wish you all a good evening.
